about: Questions asked of the planner. Each answer should spawn new questions; `unlocks` names the data that would answer an open one.

questions.question: Where should a new GP surgery go?
questions.finding: By walking distance alone: near Norton Road, St Peters (~3,900 households brought within 15 min).

questions.question: Does being far from a GP actually harm people's health?
questions.finding: No sign of it. After age and deprivation, GP walking distance shows no link with Census 2021 bad health or disability across 64 neighbourhoods. Deprivation explains most of the difference (r = 0.91).

questions.question: Can people actually get an appointment? Which surgeries are over capacity?
questions.unlocks: NHS Digital: patients registered per GP practice, GP workforce (FTE GPs per practice)

questions.question: Why is health worst around Selsey Close and Windermere Drive, when a GP is 12–18 min away?
questions.unlocks: Index of Multiple Deprivation (income, employment, housing), access to green space, fast-food density, air quality

questions.question: Do older people in Lower Wick (35% over 65, 38 min walk to a GP) have a bus or car to get there?
questions.unlocks: Census 2021 car availability (TS045); bus timetables (Bus Open Data) for real public-transport times
questions.finding: Mostly yes. Worcester 012E (Lower Wick, around Montreal Close): 34% over 65, 15% of households have no car (city 20%). About 1 household in 7 there relies on walking 38 min or the bus. 012D: 10% no car.

questions.question: Should 'best site' be ranked by need (health, age, deprivation) instead of just households within walking distance?
questions.unlocks: A need score per neighbourhood from data already loaded; change rankChanges to weight by need
questions.finding: Yes, and it changes the answer. Weighting each household by its neighbourhood's need (bad health, over-65s, deprivation, no car) moves the best GP site from Norton Road (St Peters) to Malvern Road, St John's (WR2), west of the Severn, then Henwick (Farley Street). Census 2021 need score in census.json.

questions.question: How often do buses actually run from Lower Wick to a GP surgery?
questions.unlocks: Bus Open Data GTFS timetables (West Midlands, 207 MB, reachable): trips per hour and journey times to each surgery

questions.question: Is the west side (St John's, Dines Green, Lower Wick) cut off by the River Severn, with too few crossings?
questions.unlocks: Detour ratios already computed (access.js) split by river side; count of walkable and drivable crossings; traffic counts on the crossings

questions.question: Why do corner shops seem to do better in poorer neighbourhoods, and the opposite in well-off ones?
questions.finding: Partly true, weakly. The most deprived third of Worcester's neighbourhoods has ~1.7x the convenience shops per household (0.96 vs 0.58 per 1,000) and 2x the supermarkets. The likelier driver is car ownership, not money as such: 33% of households there have no car vs 11% in the least deprived third. Only 30 convenience shops are mapped in OSM, so treat as a hint.

questions.question: Are corner shops thriving or just surviving, and what else (takeaways, cafes, pubs) clusters with deprivation and bad health?
questions.unlocks: Food Standards Agency hygiene ratings API (reachable): every food business with type and location; opening and closing dates over time

questions.question: What should happen to County Hall, Worcester?
questions.unlocks: Site size and condition; planning.data.gov.uk (local plan, constraints, listed status); access scores for the site as homes vs offices vs a health hub; traffic on Spetchley Road; Worcestershire County Council's own estate plans

questions.question: What should we do with Worcester's empty shops?
questions.unlocks: Where they are: OSM vacant/disused shop tags (patchy), FSA closures, Valuation Office business rates list, council vacancy surveys; footfall proxies (bus stops, car parks, traffic counts); what similar towns did

questions.question: What would a 'New Worcester' look like, cyclist-friendly vs driver-friendly?
questions.unlocks: Scenarios as sets of network edits, scored on one dashboard (access, traffic, cycling, health benefit via WHO HEAT, safety via STATS19). Ties together q7, q8, q11, q12
